author: MidnightBeats
body:
This is an updated, optimized help guide for all players on Avicus.
The purpose of this thread is to
  • Help players alike create a well-detailed player report on Avicus' services
  • Learn and understand the expectations when creating a player report
  • Reduce the several other "help" threads into one guide, for ease of access
  • Clear up any confusion regarding Player Reports.
I have used multiple past sources that I will be crediting at the end for the creation of this guide.

SECTION A: Creating a Player Report on Avicus' Services

A1: Creating a Good Player Report In-Game

There are several elements to creating a good report on the Avicus Network. In this section, we will guide you in creating a good player report, and differentiating between average and mediocre examples. It is encouraged that you follow the guideline below, as it will ensure your report will be dealt with and will make our jobs a little easier.

A Good Player Report:

/report MidnightBeats Hacking - AntiKnockback - (Optional) Shot him but doesn't fall off a bridge
/report ViceWatercolour Team Grief - Spawnblocking - (Optional) Using fences

This is an example of a good player report. It is clearly organized and provides great explanation on what the player is doing wrong. As seen above, you can optionally state what exactly is happening.

An Average Player Report:

/report MidnightBeats Hacking
/report ViceWatercolour Team Grief

This is an example of an average player report. It is clearly organized but provides a rather vague explanation. Nonetheless, moderators will end up taking the report, but a more detailed report may end up higher on their priority lists.

A Poor Player Report:

/report MidnightBeats lol bad ez n0scope
/report ViceWatercolour ban him pls he is hacking!
/report Posighdun horrible mod doesn't do anything
/report Arigenn ban him you stupid mods!

These are examples of poor player reports.
The first report will earn you a bright and shiny infraction. Keep in mind that we don't find these sorts of reports funny whatsoever.
The second report provides a vague explanation, but encouraging moderators to punish the player will not help you or us.
The third report is a somewhat inconclusive report. If you have a problem with a staff member, email support@avicus.net
The fourth report will also earn you an infraction if done in excess or done severely. We don't need to hear you calling us stupid.

Remember that there are some exceptions to this system, such as self-explanatory situations.
These situations don't require much explanation at all.
This can include (but is not limited to) reports regarding profane language, harassment, etc.

A2: Creating a Good Player Report on the Forums

When it comes to creating a good player report on the forums, there's not a whole lot to it, but we do have a guideline that we will ask you to follow, for the sake of efficiency.

Format:
Name of Player being reported:
Rule broken:
Evidence:
Anything else you would like to add?

Troll reports will be ignored, and a punishment will be warranted. Don't do it!
Remember, if you are uploading a video, make it unlisted.
Title your thread appropriately, with the name of the player being reported, follow by a single word reason.

SECTION B: MISCELLANEOUS TUTORIALS / INFORMATION

B1: Expectations / Miscellaneous Guidelines

This section contains some general information that will aid players when creating a player report.

Miscellaneous Guidelines
  • Do not post a complaint about a staff member under "Report a Player." Talk to the said staff member privately to discuss the issue, or e-mail support@avicus.net
  • Always include evidence. Reports that lack evidence will be instantaneously denied.
  • Remember that the "Report a Player" Subsection is not a substitution for an in-game report. Forum reports that encourage moderators to come in-game will be ignored.
Player Reports - Expectations
  • Be clear when you provide evidence, and present yourself in a respectable manner when you create a player report.
  • We will only punish players for major offences. Minor offences will be ignored or explained to you (in the event such a situation occurs)
Hacking/Client Side Modifications
  • When reporting a player, make sure you are able to identify the type of hacked client they are using, and that it is a legitimate one. Refer to the list of illegal modifications here: avicus.net/rules
  • Evidence must be long enough in order to make a successful conclusion.
Chat
  • Reports related to chat include excessive usage of caps, profane language, advertising, and inappropriate links. Screenshots are preferred for the form of evidence.
  • Advertising includes advertising the IP addresses of Minecraft servers, websites, and other social media.
  • Inappropriate links include links containing (but not limited to) pornography, scams, screamer videos/sites, etc.
Ban Evasion
  • Ban Evasion is when a player evades their punishment through an alternate account.
  • Reports related to ban evasion may take longer to be dealt with, as only Senior Staff members can check the IP addresses of other players.
B2: Uploading an image (via imgur)

You are free to use any other image service, such as Gyazo, but this tutorial will optimize the usage of the online website, imgur.

Follow these steps below in order to add an image to a forum post.
  1. Find the image you would like to upload. Prepare it for use by placing it on your desktop, or any other folder that would make it easily accessible. For information on how to find Minecraft screenshots, please refer to the guide below, in B2.
  2. Go to http://www.imgur.com/
  3. You will find the "Upload images" button, usually on the right hand side of the screen.
  4. Click this and select "upload from PC."
  5. Find the image you wish to use, and select "Open.
  6. The upload will begin immediately
  7. Once you have uploaded the image, right-click for the Image URL (or use your address bar to copy the URL of the image) and insert it into the forums.
  8. Once you have URL copied, click the "Insert image" icon on the forums (looks like a little picture).
  9. Paste your link.
The image should now be visible, and may even take some time to load.
If the image appears as a blue question mark, you may need to add the extension ".png" at the end of the link. Simply follow steps 8-9 again and add .png after you have pasted the link.

B3: Locating a Screenshot from Minecraft

Windows

  1. Enter "%appdata%" in your search bar.
  2. Open "Roaming."
  3. Open the .minecraft folder.
  4. Locate the "screenshots" folder
  5. Locate the screenshot you want from this folder, and transfer them if necessary.
Mac

  1. Open Finder.
  2. Click "Go" at the top of the screen.
  3. Hold down the "Alt" button and open "Library."
  4. Go to the "Application Support" folder.
  5. Locate the "Minecraft" folder.
  6. Locate the "screenshots" folder.
  7. Locate the screenshots you want from this folder, and transfer them if necessary.
CREDITS

This work would not have been possible without the assistance of a few others. I used some previous, outdated sources in the creation of this guide. I have used updated information whilst creating this guide in order to increase relevancy. Though the content of the sources may be from multiple Staff / Senior Staff members, I will be crediting the creator of the post (but I will still include all Senior Staff in my thanks).

Thanks to...

Staff Members (Whether Retired or Currently Active)
- Creation of Guidelines/content within sources

Joao_Victor (NolanDalton)
- Creation of the source: "How to Submit a Good Player Report"

Givenchy_
- Creation of the source: "Making a Player Report- Format"

Sho
- Creation of the source: "How to make a detailed in-game report"

awesome_apricot
- Creation of the source: "Imgur picture adding tutorial!"

I would like to give a special thanks to all the names listed above, and any other staff members that aided in the creation of these sources. Hats off to you.
